intro: Professionals and everyday users convert megabytes per second (MB/s) to megabits per second (Mbps) when working across metric and metric standards in engineering specifications, international trade documentation, and technical measurements. One megabytes per second equals 8 megabits per second, while 1 megabits per second equals 0.125 megabytes per second. Whether you are verifying data transfer specifications on imported equipment, cross-checking technical datasheets, or scaling practical measurements, this converter applies the exact NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 reference relationship with instant precision.

faqs.question: How many megabits per second (Mbps) are in 1 megabytes per second (MB/s)?
faqs.answer: There are 8 megabits per second (Mbps) in 1 megabytes per second (MB/s), which rounds to 8 Mbps for everyday calculations. Conversely, 1 megabits per second equals 0.125 megabytes per second.

faqs.question: How do I convert megabytes per second to megabits per second (MB/s to Mbps)?
faqs.answer: To convert megabytes per second to megabits per second, use the formula: Mbps = MB/s × 8. For example, converting 10 MB/s gives 80 Mbps.

faqs.question: What is 10 megabytes per second in megabits per second?
faqs.answer: 10 megabytes per second (MB/s) equals exactly 80 megabits per second (Mbps) using standard NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 conversion factors.
